title: Insurance Claim Services Note on Advance Recoupment in the Dwelling Release
content:
An emergency advance the carrier paid on the dwelling coverage can come back out of the insured's dwelling release on an Insurance Claim Services file.

**Rule.** The advance recoupment is set as follows: when the ACV carrier payments on the dwelling coverage are at least the initial dwelling approval less its depreciation withheld less the deductible, every advance payment received on the dwelling coverage, because the carrier recoups an advance it did not deduct from the ACV payment out of the final payment; when they fall short of that figure by less than the advances, the advances less that shortfall; otherwise nothing.

The figures read are the initial dwelling approval and its withheld depreciation, the deductible recorded on the claim file, and the ACV and advance carrier payments received on the dwelling coverage.

## Input — judgement — recoupment

1. Figure: initial dwelling approval less its withheld depreciation less the deductible.
2. ACV dwelling payments at or above that figure: all dwelling advances are recouped.
3. Short of it by less than the advances: the advances less the shortfall.
4. Short by the advances or more: nothing.

*Hypothetical (approval 31000.00, withheld 4200.00, deductible 1750.00, so 25050.00; advances 2400.00):* ACV payments 25050.00 recoup 2400.00; ACV payments 24250.00, short by 800.00, recoup 1600.00; ACV payments 22650.00, short by 2400.00, recoup nothing.
